_comment: PROVIDER PLUG-IN for the `runtime-guardrails` role — the gateway shape: one policy-enforcement point on the network path in front of the model and tool endpoints. It closes a specific hole: 'the agent is guarded at runtime' is otherwise a sentence nobody owns, and the only thing that could evidence it is the agent's own account of what it declined to do — which is the assertion the control exists to remove. The gateway is outside every workload, so its decision log is not written by the thing it constrains. Read adapters/providers/runtime-guardrails/README.md before choosing: the harness cannot see this fire, only that it was chosen and that a denial was recorded when probed. To adopt: record the choice in docs/governance/provider-selection.json, copy this file to docs/governance/adapters/, point it at your gateway, and wire the fetch that fills activation_evidence.
capability: Input/output filtering, tool-use allowlisting and terminology/PII screening applied at a network chokepoint in front of the model and tool endpoints, with allow and DENY decisions logged by the gateway itself

role_fit._comment: Stated plainly so the choice is made with open eyes. Neither line argues for or against — they are the trade being accepted.
role_fit.strength: One enforcement point to configure, secure and read: the policy bundle has a single digest, the decision log has a single origin, and no workload can write to either. Policy changes apply to every caller at once rather than at each service's redeploy cadence
role_fit.limitation: IT ENFORCES ONLY WHAT IS ROUTED THROUGH IT. A caller with direct credentials to the model or tool endpoint is unenforced and leaves no denial to find, so the real control is the network policy that makes the gateway the only path — which this adapter does not evidence. Record the egress restriction alongside it, or the log describes the traffic that agreed to be inspected

reconciliation._comment: Bind the log to the policy that was actually loaded, not to the policy in the repository. A bundle edited in git and never rolled out is the gap this closes. fail_mode is carried because a gateway that fails OPEN under load has no enforcement at exactly the moment it is needed, and that is a property of the deployment, not of the policy text.

activation_evidence._comment: ADOPT: fill from a real gateway read + the negative probe. The negative probe is the decisive one — decisions_allowed proves traffic, never enforcement. Only a denial you provoked and then found in the platform's own log shows the guardrail bit.
activation_evidence.fetched_at: ADOPT: timestamp of your gateway decision-log read
activation_evidence.asserted_by: ADOPT: the gateway/service identity that emits the decision log — must NOT be the agent being constrained
activation_evidence.negative_probe: ADOPT: 'denied-and-logged' once you have sent a policy-violating request, confirmed it was refused, and found that denial in the gateway's log
activation_evidence.bypass_probe: ADOPT: 'rejected' once you have tested that a call to the model or tool endpoint that skips the gateway is refused by network policy
